title: Una colección única: las preparaciones de diatomeas de Caballero y Bellido
citation: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, “Una colección única: las preparaciones de diatomeas de Caballero y Bellido,” MNCN blog, 2015.
tags: Spain; Caballero Bellido; diatoms; 205 preparations; 202 rediscovered preparations; mounting; conservation; provenance
note: An object-centred history of Caballero's diatom preparations. The museum records a donated core collection of 205 preparations made between 1891 and 1927 and separately records 202 additional preparations found in 2014 and subsequently digitized. The two preparation groups remain distinct documentary states and are not silently summed.

title: Legado Cajal: preparaciones microscópicas histológicas
citation: CSIC Red de Bibliotecas y Archivos / Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, Legado Cajal, institutional collection state documented 2024.
tags: Spain; Madrid; Cajal; histology; 3000 original preparations; legacy; provenance; BIC
note: The Cajal Legacy explicitly includes microscopic histological preparations, of which 3,000 are identified by CSIC as originals by Cajal. The broader legacy contains more than 28,000 scientific and personal assets, but that mixed asset total is not converted into a slide count. The collection was deposited at MNCN in 2023 and declared a Bien de Interés Cultural in 2024.

title: Preparación histológica comercial: oreja de gato, membrana del tímpano, sección transversal
citation: Dr. Sigmund, commercial histological preparation, cat ear / tympanic membrane transverse section, current Espacio Cajal / Simurg object catalogue record (2026).
tags: Spain; Germany; Stuttgart; Sigmund; Carl Zeiss; commercial slide; teaching; Cajal; labels; 26x76 mm
note: A surviving commercial slide exposing an international teaching-supply chain. The 26 × 76 mm glass preparation carries a printed Prof. Dr. Sigmund / Histologia Physiologica / Stuttgart / Carl Zeiss label and a specimen description in German, French and English. The catalogue says it was possibly used by Cajal for histology teaching; that cautious attribution is preserved.

note: The historical Histoteca preserves microscopic preparations from the former Chair of Micrographic Technique and Plant/Animal Histology, including more than 800 preparations by Emilio Fernández Galiano. title: Colección de maderas: preparaciones microscópicas
citation: Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, “Colección de maderas,” current online collection state (2026).
tags: Spain; Madrid; wood anatomy; xylarium; microscopic preparations; Index Xylariorum; exchange; database
note: UPM's wood collection is explicitly built from linked macroscopic wood blocks and microscopic preparations and has grown through international Index Xylariorum exchange. Official current pages expose more than 1,300 preparations in the summary, more than 1,400 in the collection description, and 1,500 on a research-group page. These are preserved as live metadata states rather than normalized.
